title: Sam Hartman, Commanders backup QB, announced as ‘The Bachelor’
content:
ABC’s “The Bachelor” is turning to a tale as old as time by bringing in an NFL player as its leading man, announcing Washington Commanders backup quarterback Sam Hartman on Friday as its new star.

Hartman, who is on Washington’s practice squad, appeared on “Good Morning America” for the announcement after the Commanders beat the New York Giants 24-21 to save their season Thursday night.

The 27-year-old, who played college football at Wake Forest and Notre Dame, said he was uncertain about becoming “The Bachelor” when first asked, but spoke with Jesse Palmer, the former Giants quarterback-turned “Bachelor” star and now the show’s host. Hartman said Palmer gave him some “insight” into the show that convinced him to sign up.

“I know one thing: when people are saying, ‘I do,’ they don’t ask you where you met,” Hartman said. “They just ask if you want to do it forever.”

Hartman joked that his teammates gave him advice for the show but said he couldn’t share it on TV.

The Commanders signed Hartman as an undrafted free agent in 2024. He headed to the NFL after six seasons of college football — five with Wake Forest and one with Notre Dame. At Wake Forest, he led the ACC with 38 passing touchdowns in 2022.

Hartman threw for 110 TDs and 12,967 yards in five seasons with the Demon Deacons before joining Notre Dame in 2023. He added 24 touchdowns and 2,689 yards with the Fighting Irish.

Hartman is No. 5 on the Commanders’ quarterback depth chart. He has played in the preseason but never in a regular-season game.

He joins Palmer and Oakland Raiders practice squad member Colton Underwood as NFL players who became “The Bachelor.” But Hartman isn’t the first Wake Forest football player to sign up for the popular show. Tyler Cameron, who played quarterback for Wake Forest in 2013 and 2014, appeared on season 15 of “The Bachelorette” in 2019. He quickly became a fan favorite and was Bachelorette Hannah Brown’s runner-up.

Viewers wanted Cameron to become the next Bachelor, but instead, his best friend and former Wake Forest teammate, Matt James, agreed to be “The Bachelor” for season 25. James played wide receiver for the Demon Deacons for four seasons and attended a few NFL tryouts after going undrafted in 2014.

Hartman’s season of “The Bachelor” will premiere on March 21.

Correction: A previous version of this article included an incorrect reference to Sam Hartman’s time with Notre Dame. He did not play in the team’s Sun Bowl win over Oregon State.
